  "candidate_id": "geometry-negative-curvature-global-sid-v1",

  "next_item_hypothesis": "Train-only transitions exhibit strongly directed item flow: 314605 of 339519 directed transition observations have no observed reverse event (fraction 0.9266197178950221). A demonstrated failure to target is therefore Euclidean residual quantization collapsing distinct outgoing next-item branches into shared early prefixes, leaving downstream next-item ranking with less separable item identifiers. This statistic motivates but does not establish the failure; validation Hard-L1 error and prefix/collision diagnostics test whether it occurs. Stage2 builds item SIDs only; downstream T5 Stage3 ranks next items.",
  "math_definition": {
    "architecture": "For each item i, content embedding e_i is passed through the existing content encoder to h_i in R^32. Quantize h_i into exactly three residual levels, each with 256 learned code vectors a[l,k] in R^32. The one global item SID is (k[i,1],k[i,2],k[i,3]); it is not user- or event-specific.",
    "fixed_geometry": "Set c=1.0, tau=1.0, epsilon=1e-5. For c>0 define exp_c(v)=tanh(sqrt(c)*||v||)/(sqrt(c)*||v||) v, with multiplier 1 when ||v||=0. Define P_c(x)=x*min(1,(1-epsilon)/(sqrt(c)*||x||)), with scale 1 at ||x||=0. Define u_c(x,y)=2c||x-y||^2/((1-c||x||^2)(1-c||y||^2)); d_c^2(x,y)=[log1p(u_c+sqrt(u_c*(u_c+2)))]^2/c, the numerically stable arcosh(1+u) squared distance. Inputs to d must lie in the open ball; all mapped points are projected first. At c=0 define exp_0(v)=v, omit P_0 entirely because its radius (1-epsilon)/sqrt(c) is undefined, and define d_0^2(x,y)=4||x-y||^2. These are the explicit c->0 limits of the same parameterized code path; there is no separate flat implementation.",
    "residual_assignment_order": "For each item i and level l=1,2,3, initialize r[i,1]=h_i. At each level, in this exact order: map q=P_c(exp_c(r[i,l])); map every level-l code b[l,k]=P_c(exp_c(a[l,k])); assign k[i,l]=argmin over k in {1,...,256} of d_c^2(q,b[l,k]), breaking ties by smallest k; subtract in the original tangent coordinates r[i,l+1]=r[i,l]-a[l,k[i,l]]. No projection is applied after subtraction; the next level maps and projects its new residual. The level-l assigned reconstruction contribution is a[l,k[i,l]], and the complete tangent reconstruction is sum over l of those three contributions.",
    "conditioning": "No level conditions on earlier discrete codes. Residual levels condition only on the continuous residual formed by subtracting the previously assigned code vectors in level order.",
    "training_loss": "Let I be the train-split item index set and n=|I|. Let h_i in R^32 be encoder outputs, and let Q_i=sum_{l=1}^3 a[l,k[i,l]]. Define L=(1/n) sum_{i in I} [||sg(h_i)-Q_i||_2^2 + ||h_i-sg(Q_i)||_2^2], where sg is stop-gradient and the two terms are respectively codebook and commitment losses with coefficient 1.0 each; the first updates code vectors only and the second encoder only. Reduction is the item mean, with all train items included, so the group is nonempty; if I is empty the training step is skipped and loss is zero. There is no parameter-dependent target distribution: assignments are hard argmin indices computed from the current forward pass and treated as nondifferentiable constants, so no target/parameter circularity arises. Validation/test events and transitions are never used in this loss."

No validation/test behavior, future events, prediction-time user context, or batch-composition signal is used.",
